parsed.main_gap: Central set Q is mis-defined as primes dividing A; the whole argument only works (and is elsewhere stated by the author) for Q = all primes ≤ A.

errors.description: Q is defined as the primes dividing A, but every subsequent use requires Q = {primes ≤ A}: e.g. 'if all prime factors of x are at most A then σ(x)=P(x)' and 'every prime in P(x)\σ(x) is greater than A' both fail for Q={p|A} (A=15, x=18: σ(18)={3} is not good). Consequently L=∏_{p|A}p is also wrong (A=15 gives L=15, but 33 is not a term while 18 is). The author's own 'Hypotheses tested' section states the correct set, so it is a one-line repairable typo.
errors.quote:
Q=\{p:p\text{ is prime and }p\mid A\},
\qquad
\sigma(x)=P(x)\cap Q.

parsed.notes: With Q read as all primes ≤ A, the argument is coherent and complete: characterization (1), the descent construction Rp^k with the minimal-counterexample b, upward-closedness, and the counting of terms in (a_n, a_n+L] are all correct and carefully handled from n=1.
